title: Design System: open-tam GTM Landing Page

equipment-beige.displayName: Equipment Beige — painted steel chassis face

amber.displayName: Amber Signal — active indicator and cable

silk-screen.displayName: Silk-Screen Ink — printed text on equipment face

metal-hi.displayName: Brushed Metal High — nameplate and footer plate highlight

display.purpose: The product name stamped onto the brushed-metal nameplate. Appears once in the hero header.

headline.purpose: Chinese section titles inside each silkscreen module header. Weight 900 for maximum density against the beige ground.

body.purpose: Explanatory text inside modules, helper annotations, ledger notes. Noto Sans SC regular weight at comfortable reading size.

label.purpose: English sub-labels, panel-box titles (IN/OUT), gauge annotations, roadmap descriptions. Saira Condensed uppercase with wide tracking simulates silkscreen printing.

mono.purpose: All machine-output text: trace ledger entries, code signatures, CLI commands, file paths, audit logs, Dymo tag content. JetBrains Mono throughout.

shadows.name: inset-cavity
shadows.purpose: Recessed terminal blocks, socket panels, output slots, toggle switches. Simulates a physical cavity pressed into the metal face.

shadows.name: module-cast
shadows.purpose: Module containers and hero machine. Soft downward shadow suggesting the module is bolted slightly above the backing surface.

shadows.name: object-cast
shadows.purpose: Fuse, bus bar, nameplate, Dymo tags. Small hard shadows for objects sitting on the panel surface.

shadows.name: paper-cast
shadows.purpose: Paper report emerging from the output slot. Deeper shadow because the paper hangs free.

shadows.name: tty-cast
shadows.purpose: Terminal window. Deepest cast shadow on the page, suggesting a heavy CRT monitor.

shadows.name: button-ring
shadows.purpose: Red and black push-buttons. Concentric ring shadows simulate a metal bezel around a physical button.

shadows.name: jewel-glow-amber
shadows.purpose: Lit amber jewel lamps emit a colored glow halo.

shadows.name: jewel-glow-green
shadows.purpose: Lit green jewel lamps emit a colored glow halo.

shadows.name: terminal-lit-glow
shadows.purpose: Lit terminal screw heads glow amber, matching jewel treatment at smaller scale.

motion.name: cable-draw
motion.purpose: The IN cable draws on from jack to bus zone on page load and hero mouseenter. Amber stroke, 9px width.

motion.name: terminal-sequence
motion.value: setTimeout stagger 70ms per terminal, starting at 500ms after cable begins
motion.purpose: Terminal screw heads light up sequentially left-to-right, simulating the orchestrator dispatching tool calls one by one.

motion.name: lamp-blink
motion.purpose: The 'now' roadmap milestone lamp blinks to indicate active/in-progress status.

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.value: opacity 0→1, translateY 22px→0, 0.6s ease, triggered at 12% intersection threshold
motion.purpose: Modules fade in as they scroll into view. One-shot via IntersectionObserver.

motion.name: theme-knob-slide
motion.purpose: The day/night toggle knob slides between positions.

components.name: Primary Push-Button (Red)
components.description: The single primary CTA — a 64px red mushroom-head push-button with concentric metal bezel rings. Used for 'run no-key demo'.
components.css: .ds-btn-red { width: 64px; height: 64px; border-radius: 50%; border: none; cursor: pointer; background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 28%, #B3271E, #842014 62%, #4E1109); box-shadow: 0 0 0 6px #847165, 0 0 0 8px #3A3125, 0 6px 12px rgba(20,14,6,0.45), inset 0 3px 5px rgba(255,255,255,0.35); transition: transform 0.08s; } .ds-btn-red:active { transform: translateY(3px); } .ds-btn-red:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #CE7A19; outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Secondary Push-Button (Black)
components.description: A 44px black push-button for secondary actions like 'view source'. Same bezel construction at smaller scale.
components.css: .ds-btn-black { width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 50%; border: none; cursor: pointer; background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 28%, #3B352B, #14110C 70%); box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px #847165, 0 0 0 7px #3A3125, 0 4px 8px rgba(20,14,6,0.45), inset 0 2px 4px rgba(255,255,255,0.2); transition: transform 0.08s; } .ds-btn-black:active { transform: translateY(2px); } .ds-btn-black:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #CE7A19; outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Dymo Label Tag
components.description: The universal annotation device — a small paper label with mono text, stuck onto the equipment face. Used for tool names, fault modes, alert types.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-block; background: #E2D7C9; color: #2A241A; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 600; border: 1px solid #4A4234; border-radius: 2px; padding: 0.15rem 0.55rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(20,14,6,0.45); }

components.name: Silkscreen Module
components.description: The primary content container — a square panel bolted to the equipment face with crosshead screws at four corners. Header carries a number, Chinese title, and English sub-label.

components.description: A 22px glowing indicator lamp with metal bezel. Amber = active/in-progress. Part of the hero header status display.

components.name: Copper Bus Bar
components.description: The horizontal copper conductor strip connecting IN to OUT. Carries the orchestrator label and two mounting bolts.
components.html: orchestrator 运维专家
components.css: .ds-bus { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 1rem; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #7A5426, #5E4020 70%); border: 1px solid #3A2712; border-radius: 3px; padding: 0.55rem 3rem; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.35), 0 2px 5px rgba(20,14,6,0.45); } .ds-bus b { font-family: 'Saira Condensed', 'Noto Sans SC', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; font-size: clamp(1rem, 1.8vw, 1.3rem); color: #F3E7D3; text-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.5); } .ds-bolt { width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 40% 35%, #E8D9BF, #8A6B3F 70%); position: absolute; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); } .ds-bolt-l { left: 10px; } .ds-bolt-r { right: 10px; }

components.name: Screw Terminal Block
components.description: An individual terminal in the screw-terminal strip. Dark recessed block with a metallic crosshead screw and copper pin stub above. Lights up amber when active.
components.css: .ds-term { position: relative; flex: 1; min-width: 30px; height: 58px; background: #0B0A08; border-radius: 3px; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.8), 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.12); display: inline-block; margin: 0 3px; } .ds-term::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%; background: linear-gradient(45deg, transparent 44%, #171310 44% 56%, transparent 56%), radial-gradient(circle at 40% 35%, #8A7B66, #3B352B 60%, #211D16 80%); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.25), 0 1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.6); } .ds-term::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 50%; bottom: 100%; transform: translateX(-50%); width: 5px; height: 20px; border-radius: 2px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #7A5426, #CE7A19); opacity: 0.9; } .ds-term-lit::after { background: radial-gradient(circle at 40% 35%, #FFE9A8, #CE7A19 60%, #7A4A0C); box-shadow: 0 0 10px 2px rgba(232,161,61,0.55); } .ds-term-ghost { opacity: 0.35; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.5); } .ds-term-ghost::before { opacity: 0.25; }

narrative.overview:
The page is not a landing page; it is one piece of rack-mounted diagnostic equipment. Every surface belongs to a single machine: alerts are physically plugged into an IN jack panel on the left, travel through a copper bus bar in the center where tool terminals light up sequentially as the orchestrator dispatches queries, and a structured root-cause report prints from an OUT slot on the right. The hero viewport fills the entire screen with this machine — no marketing hero text, no gradient, no card grid.

Below the hero, each content section is a square silkscreen module bolted to the same equipment face — numbered (01–06), labeled in Chinese with a Saira Condensed English sub-label, secured at four corners by crosshead screws. Inside each module, the visual language continues: terminal strips become trace ledgers, gauge cells become evaluation meters, roadmap milestones become module slots with indicator lamps.

The design rejects the dark-AI three-card landing-page default entirely. There are no glass surfaces, no frosted backdrops, no large radii, no gradient meshes. Depth comes from inset panel shadows and cast shadows only. The two-theme system (day shift / night shift) swaps the equipment paint from warm beige to near-black while preserving every component relationship.
keyCharacteristics: Single-machine metaphor: the entire page is one rack unit, not a collection of sections
Silkscreen modules with crosshead screws at every corner — industrial fastening, not decorative framing
Jewel indicator lamps (radial-gradient circles with glow halos) for status: amber = active, green = complete, off = dormant
Dymo-style paper label tags for data annotations (AlertEvent, query_metrics, fault modes)
Copper bus bar as the central organizing element connecting input to output
Screw-terminal strips representing tool invocations, with sequential light-up animation
Paper report with torn/zigzag bottom edge emerging from a physical output slot
Physical push-buttons (red mushroom-head primary, black secondary) as CTAs
Fuse holder as the guardrail metaphor (whitelist + dry-run)
Day/night theme toggle presented as a physical slide switch labeled day-shift / night-shift

rules.name: The One-Signal Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only color that animates. Lit terminals glow amber, the cable draws in amber, the 'now' lamp blinks amber. No other hue pulses, transitions, or flashes.

rules.name: The Red-Button Rule
rules.body: Signal red appears on exactly one element per viewport: the primary CTA push-button. Its scarcity makes it unmissable.

rules.name: The Paint-Ground Rule
rules.body: Equipment beige must cover at least 60% of any given viewport. Terminal black, copper, and amber are insets and accents within the beige field, never competing backgrounds.

rules.name: The Stamped-Label Rule
rules.body: Every English label on the equipment face uses Saira Condensed with letter-spacing of at least 0.12em and text-transform uppercase. This simulates text stamped or silkscreened onto metal.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Any text that represents machine output must use JetBrains Mono. No exceptions. If it looks like data the machine produced, it reads in mono.

rules.name: The Flat-Panel Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. No hover elevation, no scroll-parallax depth. Shadows exist only to describe physical geometry, never to imply interactivity or hierarchy.

rules.name: The Inset-Is-Cavity Rule
rules.body: Every inset box-shadow represents a physical hole, socket, or recess. If a surface needs to look pressed-in, use inset shadow. If raised, use positive-offset cast shadow. Never mix both.

dos: Do use equipment beige (#A99883 day / #2B2620 night) as the dominant background covering at least 60% of every viewport.
Do place crosshead screws at all four corners of every module and the hero machine. Screws are 14px in modules, 18px in the hero.
Do use 2px solid borders in paint-edge color for all module outlines and header dividers.
Do render all data annotations as Dymo tags: paper background, JetBrains Mono, 2px radius, 1px border.
Do use jewel lamps (22px with bezel) for hero status and mini lamps (10px) for inline status. Amber = active, green = complete, dark = dormant.
Do keep all border-radius values at 4px or below except the TTY window (6px) and circular elements.
Do use inset box-shadows for recessed elements and positive-offset cast shadows for raised elements.
Do animate only amber elements: cable draw-on, sequential terminal light-up (70ms stagger), and the 'now' roadmap lamp blink (1.6s cycle).
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — disable all animations and transitions.
Do present the day/night theme as a physical slide switch labeled 日班/夜班.
Do use Saira Condensed (uppercase, 0.12em+ tracking) for English labels, Noto Sans SC 900 for Chinese headlines, JetBrains Mono for machine-output text.
donts: Don't use border-radius larger than 6px anywhere. No pill shapes, no fully-rounded cards.
Don't use glassmorphism, backdrop-filter, frosted overlays, or any transparency-based depth effect.
Don't use gradient backgrounds that aren't vertical paint gradients or brushed-metal repeating-linear-gradients.
Don't use signal red (#842014) for anything other than the primary CTA button and the audit-log DENY marker.
Don't add hover-elevation effects to modules or cards. Only push-buttons respond to interaction.
Don't use drop shadows lighter than rgba(20,14,6,0.45) in day mode or rgba(0,0,0,0.6) in night mode.
Don't introduce colors outside the established palette. Every hue maps to a physical material.
Don't use sans-serif fonts other than Saira Condensed and Noto Sans SC. Don't use monospace other than JetBrains Mono.
Don't make the hero shorter than 100vh on desktop. The machine fills the viewport.
Don't use emoji, icon libraries, or decorative illustrations. All visuals are CSS gradients, borders, pseudo-elements, and inline SVG.
